text:
alex: quick postmortem follow-up from this morning's hotpath OOM. summary: shard residency growth from long-lived streams + delayed eviction, fragmentation spikes on 48GB nodes. listing proposed remediation + owners. :spiral_notepad:

maria: thanks — can we get the short actionable checklist here so infra can plan a patch release? :thumbsup:

sahil: adding initial profiling notes: heap snapshot at t0 shows +1.2GB per hour in cached kv segments, jemalloc retained > rss by ~10%. suspect stale refs from stream session cleanup. I'll upload profiles to the perf bucket.

jun: logs snippet I grabbed from the pod before OOM: ```
2026-02-14T09:03:12Z ERROR runtime: allocation failed: cannot allocate 512MB
pid=2345 mem_used=47.8GB rss=48.2GB frag=9%
```

alex: action items (short):
- A1: run full jemalloc arena dump & distributed heap scan on recent canaries — owner: @sahil — due: 2026-02-18
- A2: add hard softlimit for shard-residency (evict after 30m idle) in canary configs — owner: @maria — due: 2026-02-17
- A3: implement incremental KV compaction pass to shrink fragment slots (runtime patch) — owner: @jun — due: 2026-02-24
- A4: add metric for "kv_stale_sessions" and alert at 1000+ — owner: @ops-runbook — due: 2026-02-16
- A5: emergency rollback plan doc and rollout gates for canary -> prod if GC regressions show — owner: @alex — due: 2026-02-15

sahil: I started A1 — uploading jemalloc dumps to gs://redwood-perf/oom/1767770000/ now. also will attach flamegraphs.

maria: A2 note: will push canary config change to staging first; this only flips eviction policy for shards older than 30m, TTL only. no model change.

jun: A3 question: do we prefer a background compaction thread or opportunistic on-request compaction? background seems safer for steady-state but we need to measure CPU cost. leaning background with token-bucket rate limit.

alex: prefer background with cap for now. add a feature flag. ensure it respects dedicated pool QoS.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: canary config change scheduled for 2026-02-16 03:00 UTC (staging) by maria. CI: green. :robot_face:

maria: tagging a small test plan: 
- create 50 long-lived stream sessions (10m-60m) on staging
- monitor kv_residency_size, kv_fragmentation, jemalloc.retained_bytes
- run for 6 hours, capture heap dumps every hour

ops-runbook: added alert runbook entry: "hotpath OOM pulse" -> run A1, check kv_stale_sessions, escalate to eng-runtime-sre if trend > +20%/hr. documented steps and Slack escalation template.

alex: quick risk notes: compaction could spike tail latency on small nodes. plan: rollout with rate-limit and a canary percent (5% of traffic), and measure p95. if p95 > baseline+20ms rollback.

sahil: uploaded artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/oom/1767770000/{jemalloc.dmp,heap-flame-1.svg,heap-flame-2.svg}. I'll attach quick diff with previous stable run.

maria: assigning myself to validation of A2 after staging deploy. will post results here.

jun: starting prototype of compaction worker today, will open PR with feature flag and benchmark harness. ETA for PR: 2026-02-19.

alex: meet sync: let's reconvene Friday 2026-02-19 16:00 UTC for a status check (30m). agenda: A1 results, staging A2 metrics, compaction perf numbers.

maria: ack.

sahil: ack, will have heatmap and heap diffs ready.

jun: ack, will demo compaction harness.

alex: thanks all. small reminder: when you push config or runtime changes, add a single-line backward-compatible fallback so we can toggle quickly. :memo:

maria: noted, will include rollback flag.

sahil: one more quick note — if we see jemalloc retained >> rss that's a sign of fragmentation; we should prioritize compaction over more aggressive eviction until we have data.

alex: agree. ops-runbook, please include that heuristic in the runbook steps.

ops-runbook: added heuristic: "if jemalloc.retained_bytes / rss > 1.08 -> flag fragmentation priority".

alex: closing for now. please update the thread when you hit the due dates or blockers. :white_check_mark:
